data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["A compliant panel's output is a function of the cue; a reliable panel's output is a function of the answer-generating structure.","Compliance can be detected by cue-answer decorrelation; reliability cannot.","A compliant panel is brittle under cue manipulation; a reliable panel is robust."],"overturn_conditions":["If the checklist's cues are inseparable from the causal structure, the decorrelation test cannot be constructed.","If the panel ignores the checklist entirely, the test does not evaluate the checklist's contribution."],"shared_structure":["Both the compliant and reliable panel produce outputs from inputs.","Both can be tested by manipulating the correlation between cues and answers.","Both are subject to the same objective outcome metric."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_002","SRC_004"],"transfer_claims":["From causal inference: an intervention that breaks the correlation between a cue and its outcome reveals whether a system relies on the cue or on the underlying causal structure.","From adversarial evaluation: perturbing inputs while holding labels constant tests robustness of a model's decision boundary."]},"claim":"Within a single evaluation, the evidence that distinguishes genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance is whether the panel's accuracy remains high when the checklist's superficial cues are inverted or held constant while the underlying correct answer changes. Genuine gain requires the panel to track the answer, not the cue; mere compliance tracks the cue regardless of the answer.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the checklist's cues are inseparable from the answer-generating structure, decorrelation is impossible and the test cannot be applied.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the panel adapts by ignoring the checklist and guessing, the decorrelation test may falsely indicate genuine gain.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert also relies on the same surface cues, the test fails to distinguish panel from expert.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Mere compliance means the panel follows the checklist's visible cues to an answer. If the cues are decorrelated from the answer (e.g., by holding the cue constant while varying the answer), a merely compliant panel will produce the same output for all cases, while a genuinely reliable panel will adapt.
